source_review.notes: Checked current primary Linux-kernel documentation for locking contexts, lock types, memory barriers, spinlocks, atomic types, lockdep, lockstat, KCSAN, RCU, sequence counters, reference counting, mutexes, plus MIT's 2025 xv6 text. All 13 cited URLs returned HTTP 200; configuration-specific and PREEMPT_RT semantics are attributed and bounded.

notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates invariant protection, caller context, memory ordering, dependency graph, performance observations, and object lifetime.

evidence: Executed the graph model and confirmed A-to-B and B-to-C form an acyclic base order.
Confirmed adding C-to-A produces the reported cycle A->B->C->A.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic graph has three static classes and omits runtime lock semantics, timing, IRQ state, and conditional acquisition.

evidence: Re-derived that a simple global-order proof requires the directed lock-class graph to be acyclic.
Traced enter, exclusive access, temporary invariant opening, restoration, publication, exit, and separate lifetime closure for shared object O.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Acyclic class order addresses one deadlock condition; it does not prove progress, context admissibility, ordering, or lifetime.

evidence: Reviewed process, preemption, hard IRQ, soft IRQ, NMI-like, work-queue, timer, callback, remote-CPU, tracing, error, and teardown access paths.

boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Context, order, memory, progress, lifecycle, configuration, scalability, security, real-time, and assurance boundaries receive separate treatment.

evidence: Traced documented ownership, complete access-path coverage, context admissibility, acyclic acquisition, publication, lifetime, and configuration invariants through ten examples and five answers.
Verified the cycle detector preserves visit state and reports only a back edge into the current recursion stack.

evidence: Reviewed invariant definition, accessor enumeration, protocol selection, publication, global dependency order, progress, lifetime closure, and multi-tool evidence.

evidence: Audited uses of atomic, exclusive, ordered, safe, valid, acyclic, lock-free, bounded, real-time, and certification.
